newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity futures end mixed, mostly lower.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity futures end mixed, mostly lower.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures ended mixed though mostly lower Monday as traders watched Western weather forecasts to give the market some direction, industry sources said.
"We could see some more strength in the November session if we get some good (cold) weather out here," said one Western futures trader.
Weather in the Northwest was forecast to be below normal from October 17 to 21, with normal temperatures expected in the Southwest through the same period.
November Califorinia-Oregon Border (COB) futures ended up one cent at $17.06 after trade as high as $17.20 per megawatt hour (MWh), while December finished up five cents at the day's high of $18.60.
November Palo Verde (PV) settled down 12 cents at $16.48 per MWh from trade as low as $16.00, while December finished down 16 cents at $16.75 from a session low of $16.70.
Remaining PV deferreds were down between five and 15 cents.
NYMEX said an estimated total of 313 COB and 178 PV contracts traded Monday.
COB open interest for October 11 rose one to 3,921, while PV open interest rose 55 to 1,374, NYMEX said.
-- Chris Reese, New York Power Desk 212-859-1627
